title: Crop Insurance Agency Training Notes on Projected and Harvest Prices and Optional Provisions
content:
**Rule.** For Crop Insurance the projected price is set by the product's projected price basis and the harvest price by its harvest price basis, both released by RMA and recorded unchanged for every policy of the crop; neither is negotiated or estimated by the agency. Catastrophic coverage uses the projected price only. Yield substitution, trend adjustment, quality adjustment and the hail and fire exclusion apply only where the product's switch is true, and production records must be kept for the product's records-retention period in years.

When RMA releases the harvest price for a crop year, it is recorded on each policy record of the crop.

## Questions answered

**Where does a policy's projected price come from?**
From the product's projected price basis, as released by RMA. The agency records it unchanged; it does not negotiate or estimate it.

**Does the agency give its own estimate of the harvest price before the release?**
No. The harvest price is set by the product's harvest price basis and released by RMA; the agency neither negotiates nor estimates it.

**Two members grow the same crop. Can their policies carry different harvest prices?**
No. Both prices are recorded unchanged for every policy of the crop, so every policy of that crop carries the same released price.

**Which price does a Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) policy use?**
The projected price only.

**When do yield substitution, trend adjustment, quality adjustment or the hail and fire exclusion apply?**
Only where the product's switch for that provision is true at the member's plan and coverage level. Where the switch is not true, the provision does not apply.

**How long are production records kept?**
For the product's records-retention period, stated in years.
